text: anytime that you're interacting with a model and you're asking it to do really advanced things, and it's not performing your expectations, like somewhere there's probably an expert...working directly for the best researchers in the world.
speaker: Garrett Lord
context: Lenny asks if there's anything else about the data labeling field that people don't fully understand. Garrett explains how AI labs are constantly working to improve model performance across different domains. When users experience limitations with AI models in advanced areas, there are likely domain experts already working with top researchers at frontier AI labs to address those specific weaknesses through a scientific process of iteration and improvement.
text_ko: 모델(model)과 상호작용하면서 정말 고도화된 작업(advanced tasks)을 시키는데 기대만큼 수행하지 못하면, 어딘가에는 아마 세계 최고의 연구진(best researchers in the world)을 위해 직접 일하는 전문가(expert)가 있을 거예요.
text_zh: 每次你在使用模型，让它做一些特别高难度的事情，结果它的表现没达到你的预期时，很可能在某个地方就有专家...直接为世界顶尖的研究人员工作。
text_es: cada vez que trabajas con un modelo y le pides que haga cosas muy avanzadas, y no te está dando los resultados que esperas, en algún lugar probablemente hay un experto... trabajando directamente con los mejores investigadores del mundo.
key_sentence: somewhere there's probably an expert...working directly for the best researchers in the world.
original_text: Generally speaking, anytime that you're interacting with a model and you're asking it to do really advanced things, and it's not performing your expectations, like somewhere there's probably an expert that is the top mind in that domain working directly for the best researchers in the world at the Frontier Labs trying to understand and go through the scientific iteration process of how to make that better.

vocabulary.definition: The act of communicating or engaging with someone or something, often involving a reciprocal exchange.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, interacting often refers to the way users engage with software, models, or systems to achieve desired outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'interacting' implies a two-way communication, it can also suggest varying levels of engagement, from passive observation to active participation.

vocabulary.definition: Executing a task or function, particularly in a manner that meets or exceeds established standards or expectations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, performing often relates to the effectiveness of employees, systems, or technologies in achieving specific goals or metrics.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'performing' can carry a positive connotation when results are favorable, but may imply failure or inadequacy when expectations are not met.

vocabulary.definition: A person who possesses a high level of knowledge or skill in a particular area, often recognized by peers or industry standards.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, experts are often sought for their specialized knowledge to inform decision-making, guide projects, or provide training.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'expert' suggests a depth of experience and authority, but can also imply a narrow focus; it's important to specify the area of expertise.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals or groups engaged in systematic investigation to establish facts, gather information, or develop new insights in a specific field.
vocabulary.businessContext: Researchers in business and technology often contribute to innovation, product development, and market analysis by providing data-driven insights.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'researchers' typically denotes a formal role within academia or industry, it can also imply a broader group of individuals involved in inquiry and analysis.

text: the only moat in human data is access to an audience.
speaker: Garrett Lord
context: Lenny asks about Scale AI being acquired by Meta and whether this creates opportunities for other companies in the data labeling space. Garrett explains why AI labs prefer working with independent data providers rather than competitors. He emphasizes that in the human data labeling business, the key competitive advantage is having direct access to the right experts, rather than relying on expensive recruitment and advertising to find qualified people.
text_ko: 사람들에 관한 데이터(human data)에서 유일한 해자(moat)는 결국 오디언스(audience)에 대한 접근뿐이에요.
text_zh: 在人类数据这块，唯一的护城河就是能不能接触到用户群体。
text_es: El único diferenciador real en datos humanos es tener acceso a una audiencia.
key_sentence: the only moat in human data is access to an audience.
original_text: I think if you viewed your research team and your model building team, and the experiments they're running to be really the cornerstone of how you're improving, you probably wouldn't want the latest research of what you're trying to work on being invested in by a peer. We like to say the only moat in human data is access to an audience.

vocabulary.definition: A moat is a protective barrier, often a physical or metaphorical one, that safeguards a business from competition. In business, it refers to unique advantages that prevent competitors from easily entering the market.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, a moat can include intellectual property, brand loyalty, or proprietary technology that gives a company a competitive edge.
vocabulary.nuance: While traditionally associated with physical barriers, in business it often implies strategic advantages that are not easily replicable.

vocabulary.definition: Access refers to the ability or right to approach, enter, or use something. It signifies the availability of resources or information to individuals or organizations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, access often pertains to the ability to utilize data, tools, or networks that can enhance operational efficiency and decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: Access can imply both privilege and restriction, depending on the context, and is often discussed in relation to data privacy and security.

vocabulary.definition: An audience is a group of individuals who receive or engage with content, products, or services. It represents the target demographic for communication and marketing efforts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and advertising, understanding the audience is crucial for tailoring messages and strategies that resonate and drive engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a passive group of listeners or viewers, but in a business context, it often refers to an active participant in the brand experience.

text: we built a decade of trust with 18 million people, and they trust us, and we built a ton of brand affinity.
speaker: Garrett Lord
context: Garrett explains why Handshake has been so successful in the data labeling market compared to competitors. While other companies spend millions on advertising and recruiting to find experts, Handshake leveraged their existing decade-old platform that already had relationships with 18 million students and professionals. This existing trust and detailed user profiles gave them a massive competitive advantage in quickly scaling their expert network.
text_ko: 우리는 10년 동안 1,800만 명과 신뢰를 쌓아왔고, 그들이 우리를 믿어줘요. 덕분에 브랜드 호감도(brand affinity)도 크게 쌓였어요.
text_zh: 我们花了十年时间赢得了1800万用户的信任，他们真的很信任我们，而且我们的品牌粘性特别强。
text_es: Construimos una década de confianza con 18 millones de personas, confían en nosotros, y logramos una conexión muy fuerte con la marca.
key_sentence: we built a decade of trust with 18 million people, and they trust us
original_text: The huge advantage that we've had and why we've resonated so fast in the marketplace is we built a decade of trust with 18 million people, and they trust us, and we built a ton of brand affinity, and they use Handshake, and they have an active profile, and we have a ton of information around their academic performance and what they've done in school.

vocabulary.definition: Brand affinity refers to the emotional connection and loyalty that consumers feel towards a particular brand, often resulting in repeat purchases and advocacy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in marketing and branding, fostering brand affinity is crucial for building long-term customer relationships and enhancing brand equity.
vocabulary.nuance: While brand affinity suggests a positive emotional bond, it should not be confused with mere brand awareness, which indicates recognition without emotional attachment.

vocabulary.definition: Trust is the firm belief in the reliability, truth, or ability of someone or something, often forming the foundation of relationships and transactions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, trust is essential for establishing partnerships, customer loyalty, and effective team dynamics, as it influences decision-making and collaboration.
vocabulary.nuance: Trust can be fragile and takes time to build, but it can be quickly eroded by negative experiences or breaches of confidence.

vocabulary.definition: Built refers to the process of constructing or developing something, often implying a foundation or groundwork laid over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'built' often relates to the development of systems, relationships, or brands, indicating a deliberate and sustained effort to create value.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'built' conveys a sense of permanence and effort, distinguishing it from terms like 'created' which may imply a more transient or less substantial process.

text: We're the largest expert network in the world. We have more PhDs, 500,000 of them use Handshake than any other platform. We have three million master students who are in school or alumni.
speaker: Garrett Lord
context: Garrett describes how Handshake discovered the opportunity in AI data labeling. As the demand shifted from generalist workers to experts for training AI models, companies began approaching Handshake to recruit from their massive network of PhD and master's degree holders. This led them to realize they could cut out these middleman companies and serve the AI labs directly while providing a better experience for their users.
text_ko: 저희는 전 세계에서 가장 큰 전문가 네트워크(expert network)이에요. 박사 학위자들(PhDs)이 어느 플랫폼보다 많고, 그중 50만 명이 Handshake 플랫폼(Handshake)을 사용해요. 재학 중이거나 동문인 석사생(master students)이 300만 명 있어요.
text_zh: 我们是全球最大的专家网络平台。我们这里的博士最多，有50万博士在用Handshake，比其他任何平台都多。我们还有300万硕士用户，有在校的也有校友。
text_es: Somos la red de expertos más grande del mundo. Tenemos más doctores, 500,000 de ellos usan Handshake, más que cualquier otra plataforma. Y tenemos tres millones de estudiantes de maestría, tanto actuales como egresados.
key_sentence: We have more PhDs, 500,000 of them use Handshake than any other platform.
original_text: We're the largest expert network in the world. We have more PhDs, 500,000 of them use Handshake than any other platform. We have three million master students who are in school or alumni. And so, we started to see all what I would call middleman companies reaching out to us saying, 'Can we recruit your PhDs and master's students?'

vocabulary.definition: An expert network is a platform that connects businesses with industry specialists who provide insights and advice based on their expertise. These networks facilitate knowledge sharing and help organizations make informed decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, expert networks are often utilized for market research, product development, and strategic planning, allowing companies to tap into specialized knowledge that may not be readily available internally.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'expert network' conveys a sense of exclusivity and high-level expertise, making it suitable for discussions about specialized consulting services but less appropriate for general networking contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Alumni are individuals who have graduated from a particular institution, especially a school or university. They often maintain connections with their alma mater and can play a role in its community and activities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, alumni networks can be valuable for recruiting, mentorship, and fostering partnerships, as former students often have a shared experience and can support each other's professional endeavors.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'alumni' typically refers to graduates, it carries a connotation of loyalty and ongoing engagement with the institution, making it more suitable in formal or community-focused discussions.

text: There will never be a time like this. I've never seen anything like it. I doubt I'll ever feel anything like this in business again where there's unlimited demand. How do you make sure that three months from now, six months, you have no regrets?
speaker: Garrett Lord
context: Garrett shares the motto 'leave nothing to chance' that his team adopted while building their AI data labeling business. He emphasizes the unprecedented nature of the current AI opportunity, where there's essentially unlimited demand for high-quality training data. This mindset drove his team to work extremely hard - including nights and weekends - to ensure they could capitalize on this once-in-a-lifetime market opportunity.
text_ko: 이런 기회는 다시 없을 거예요. 이런 건 본 적이 없어요. 무한한 수요(unlimited demand)가 있는 상황을 사업에서 다시 경험할 것 같지 않아요. 3개월, 6개월 뒤에 후회가 없으려면 어떻게 해야 할까요?
text_zh: 这种机会真的是千载难逢。我从来没见过这样的情况。我觉得在商业上可能再也不会遇到这种需求无限大的时候了。你怎么确保三个月后、六个月后，不会后悔没抓住这个机会？
text_es: No va a haber otro momento como este. Nunca he visto algo así. Dudo que vuelva a vivir algo parecido en los negocios, donde hay demanda ilimitada. ¿Cómo te aseguras de que dentro de tres meses, seis meses, no te vayas a arrepentir?
key_sentence: I doubt I'll ever feel anything like this in business again where there's unlimited demand.
original_text: There will never be a time like this. I've never seen anything like it. I doubt I'll ever feel anything like this in business again where there's unlimited demand. How do you make sure that three months from now, six months, you have no regrets? Get on the plane to go talk to a customer, make the late night push, check the data six times over again.

vocabulary.definition: The desire of consumers to purchase goods or services at a given price.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding demand is crucial for inventory management, pricing strategies, and forecasting sales, as it directly influences revenue potential.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply urgency or necessity, particularly when discussing market conditions where demand exceeds supply.

vocabulary.definition: Feelings of sadness or disappointment over something that has happened or been done, especially a missed opportunity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'regrets' often refer to decisions made or opportunities missed that could have led to better outcomes, emphasizing the importance of strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a reflective connotation, suggesting a desire to learn from past experiences to avoid similar feelings in the future.

text: That's not what we're hearing from our employers, this is just enabling human beings to be even more productive. You used to put a Google Search on a skill on your resume because you grew up with Google.
speaker: Garrett Lord
context: Lenny asks about the tension between students training AI models that might eventually replace entry-level jobs. Garrett pushes back on fears about job displacement, explaining that employers using Handshake aren't reducing hiring. Instead, AI is making workers more productive, similar to how previous generations became skilled with Google search. He argues that young people who grow up using AI tools naturally will have significant advantages in the job market.
text_ko: 우리가 고용주들로부터 듣는 얘기는 그게 아니에요. 이건 단지 사람들이 훨씬 더 생산적으로 일할 수 있게 해주는 도구일 뿐이에요. 예전에는 구글과 함께 자랐기 때문에 이력서(resume)에 '구글 검색(Google Search)' 같은 스킬을 적곤 했어요.
text_zh: 但我们从雇主那里听到的不是这个意思，这其实是让人变得更有效率。以前你会在简历上写"会用谷歌搜索"这样的技能，因为你是伴随着谷歌长大的。
text_es: Pero no es eso lo que nos dicen las empresas, esto simplemente permite que las personas sean aún más productivas. Antes ponías "búsquedas en Google" como habilidad en tu currículum porque creciste con Google.
key_sentence: this is just enabling human beings to be even more productive.
original_text: That's not what we're hearing from our employers, this is just enabling human beings to be even more productive. You used to put a Google Search on a skill on your resume because you grew up with Google. Being AI native, young people are at a huge advantage.

vocabulary.definition: Providing the means or opportunity for something to happen or be achieved.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'enabling' often refers to tools, processes, or systems that facilitate greater efficiency or capability within an organization.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'enabling' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply a degree of dependency if overused.

vocabulary.definition: Yielding favorable or significant results, especially in terms of output or efficiency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'productive' often describes employees, processes, or technologies that maximize output and contribute positively to organizational goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can sometimes imply a focus on quantity over quality, so context is important when using it.
